uncited: Texture streaming is a technique for rendering 4D volumetric data (3D spatial dimensions + time) when the total volume exceeds available graphics memory.
It solves the memory constraint by allocating a single 3D texture and sequentially uploading individual timesteps from main memory to the GPU for each frame.
Unlike caching all timesteps in VRAM, this method trades increased CPU-GPU bus traffic for reduced graphics memory usage.
- Set texture parameters (wrap modes, filtering) using `glTexParameteri`.
- Upload the first timestep (`pData[0]`) to the GPU using `glTexImage3D`.
- Increment `curTimeStep` and wrap it around: `curTimeStep = (curTimeStep + 1) % numTimesteps`.
- Upload the current timestep's data (`pData[curTimeStep]`) to the existing texture storage using `glTexSubImage3D`.
This overwrites the previous timestep's data in place.
- Execute the drawing code (ray marching or similar) which samples from the bound texture.
- **Time Complexity:** $O(1)$ per frame for texture upload, but dependent on the bandwidth of the CPU-GPU bus.
The cost is proportional to the size of one timestep's volume data.
- **Memory Complexity:** $O(V)$ where $V$ is the size of a single 3D volume, regardless of the number of timesteps.
This is significantly lower than caching all timesteps ($O(T \times V)$).
- **Limitations:** High CPU-GPU bus traffic; potential frame rate reduction due to data transfer latency; not suitable for real-time interaction if the transfer time exceeds the frame budget.
- **When to use:** When graphics memory is insufficient to hold all timesteps simultaneously, but the dataset fits in main RAM.
- **When not to use:** When low latency and high frame rates are critical, or when the dataset fits entirely in VRAM (caching is preferred).
